correctness.rationale: The index-three A sites have Voronoi regular hexagons of circumradius one; six B sites lie at the vertices and all other B sites are farther from every central-hexagon point. Thus full plane coverage is equivalent to radial A disks of radius r covering the B-uncovered part of one hexagon. For s≤1/2 the maximal B-uncovered radial norm is sqrt(1−s+s²); for 1/2≤s≤1, a polar ray at angle π/6 gives (sqrt3−sqrt(4s²−1))/2; for s≥1 B disks alone cover. The exact all-point geometry, including equality at s=1/2 and s=1, supports F(s), not the finite Monte Carlo. Two strictly convex/unimodal branch costs have unique interior minima at s1=1/(2c), s2=(1/2)sqrt(1+3/c²) with E1,E2; E2−E1=(c−2−2/c)/4 yields sole c*=1+sqrt3 and exactly two distinct minimizers, derivative jump 1/2+1/c*². Independently checked algebra, stationary derivatives, and bounded grid only as corroboration. Applies to fixed index-three coloring and w>0, not arbitrary sensor positions.
residual_risks: Geometric reduction must be retained; a finite lattice patch cannot certify global coverage independently of nearest-site geometry.
